clue.text: Vigorous musical — caught song lacking body

parts.note: Mus. is the standard abbreviation for music or musical, as in the degree MusB
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the body of a word is its middle, so the central letter of the song word goes

parts.note: a lay is an old word for a song or ballad

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a lively stage show whose captured song turned out hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking body' takes the middle A out of LAY, leaving LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone muscly is strong and brawny, hence vigorous in build and action.

clue.text: University writing on principally dandy thing duck does

parts.note: to pen is to write, so the noun pen stands in for writing

indicators.note: principally means chiefly or first, so only the opening letter of dandy is wanted

explanation.surface: An undergraduate's essay on what is essentially a dandy, which turns out to be about ducks.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' simply puts one piece above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: A dabbling duck tips itself bottom-up to feed, which is to upend.

clue.text: Progressive increase of intensity of last part in rough soccer

indicators.note: in places the last-part word inside the rearranged letters
rough play suggests the letters of soccer are knocked about into a new order

parts.note: the end is the last part of anything

explanation.surface: A commentator notes rough soccer getting steadily more intense towards the final stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' gives CRESCO; the term comes from music, where it marks a passage getting gradually louder.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescendo is a musical term for a gradual swelling in loudness, used generally for any mounting intensity.

clue.text: Indeed pig pen's restless and turbulent

parts.note: yea is an old word for yes or indeed
a sty is an enclosure where pigs are kept

explanation.surface: Truly, the pigs in their enclosure are restless and stirring.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeasty, like fermenting dough, describes something frothy, agitated and unsettled.

clue.text: Possibly grating tasks in establishment for smelting

definitions.meaning: a grating is one example of decorative or structural iron metalwork
the jobs done at an ... are its ...

explanation.surface: Perhaps the irritating jobs one gets in a foundry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks grating as an example rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironwork means articles made of iron, such as railings and gratings, and also the work of making them.

clue.text: I enter for merest tweaks in measuring instruments

indicators.note: tweaks are small adjustments, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A technician tinkering slightly with sensitive lab apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: Interferometers are scientific devices that measure lengths or wavelengths using interference of waves.

clue.text: Elite athlete's cunning main ploy

indicators.note: cunning suggests craftily twisting things, so the letters of main ploy are reworked

explanation.surface: A top sportsman's chief tactic is guile.
explanation.definitionFit: An Olympian is a competitor at the Olympic Games, the top tier of athletics.

clue.text: Distort women's pugilism

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women, as on clothing sizes
the ring stands for boxing as a sport

explanation.surface: A sneer that women's boxing is a twisted version of the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: To wring is to twist or contort something, so it can mean distort.

clue.text: Voted in again, chosen in advance with private secretary dropped separately

indicators.note: the two letters of the secretary's abbreviation are removed from two different places

parts.note: preselected means picked beforehand
PS is the abbreviation for a private secretary

explanation.surface: A politician returned to office after being lined up early, minus their aide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped separately' removes the P from the start and the S from the middle of PRESELECTED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be re-elected is to win a further term in office by another vote.

clue.text: Appropriately, bank covers part of Mediterranean

indicators.note: covers means the bank word wraps around the region

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
the Levant is the eastern Mediterranean region

explanation.surface: A shore fittingly hems in a stretch of the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is a verb here, as in bank on.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak relevantly is to speak pertinently, in a way suited to the matter in hand.

clue.text: Chopped into cubes, trimmed and frozen

indicators.note: trimmed means cut back, here losing the front letter

parts.note: diced food is cut into small cubes

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: dice it, trim it and freeze it.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced means covered with or turned to ice, so frozen.

clue.text: Pedagogue's old coin in European gold

indicators.note: in puts the coin inside the other pieces

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
the ducat was a gold coin once used across Europe

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster's antique coin set in European gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedagogue is a teacher, and an educator is one who teaches.

clue.text: Mark on prosthesis

parts.note: a peg can serve as a marker, as in cribbage scoring
in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: A scratch or label on an artificial limb.
explanation.walkthrough: The ON = LEG equivalence comes from cricket, where the batter's leg side is called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A peg leg is a simple wooden artificial leg, an old form of prosthesis.

clue.text: Indication of guns primarily involved in offence

indicators.note: involved in places that letter inside the offence word

parts.note: a sin is a moral offence

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of guns

explanation.surface: Evidence that firearms were mainly behind the crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign is a mark or token that indicates something.

clue.text: Fine fable curiously inexpressible

indicators.note: curiously suggests something oddly arranged, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lovely fairy tale whose charm oddly defies words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ineffable describes something too great or extreme to be put into words.

clue.text: Appraise cooked veal you consumed, we're told

indicators.note: cooked suggests the meat word is prepared into a new shape, its letters rearranged
we're told signals that the word you is taken by how it is said

parts.note: you is pronounced like the letter U
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A diner is invited to judge the veal they have just eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' turns VEAL into EVAL; 'we're told' applies only to 'you', giving U.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate is to assess or judge the worth of something, which is what appraise means.

clue.text: Insufficiently value German and Irish lines

parts.note: und is German for and
Erse is an old name for the Irish Gaelic language
LL is the abbreviation for lines, as l is for one line

explanation.surface: Underestimating the worth of German and Irish railway lines.
explanation.definitionFit: To undersell is to understate the merits of something, valuing it too low.

clue.text: Holy tree around India exemplifies subgroups in species

indicators.note: around means the tree word wraps the letter for India

parts.note: the bo tree is the sacred fig under which the Buddha found enlightenment
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to typify something is to exemplify it, so types means exemplifies

explanation.surface: A sacred tree near India serves as a model of variation within a species.
explanation.definitionFit: A biotype is a group of organisms sharing the same genetic makeup, a subdivision within a species.

clue.text: Cry of exhilaration over child, say, returning

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
a minor is a child in law
eg, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: A shout of delight from a kid coming back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses O MINOR EG. The cry is what parachutists traditionally shout on jumping.
explanation.definitionFit: Geronimo is a shout of excitement given when leaping or plunging into something exhilarating.

clue.text: Strange echoes surrounding old fogey

indicators.note: surrounding means the strange word encloses the letter for old
an echo bounces back, so the letters are sent back in reverse

parts.note: odd means strange

explanation.surface: Peculiar sounds bouncing around a stuffy old person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'echoes' sends ODD back as DDO, which then goes around O. 'old fogey' looks like the whole definition, but 'old' is needed for its letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodo is an informal term for someone hopelessly old-fashioned, after the extinct bird.

clue.text: Plaything sent up to a Japanese city

parts.note: a toy is a plaything

indicators.note: sent up in a down clue means the short word is turned to read upwards

explanation.surface: A toy dispatched to a city in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: Toyota City in Aichi Prefecture is named after the carmaker based there.

clue.text: Hard work requiring energy and force in proportion to time

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
F is the physics symbol for force
for can mean considering or relative to, as in tall for his age
T is the symbol for time

explanation.surface: A physics definition of work, built from energy, force and time.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a physics formula, but each quantity is just its symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Effort is strenuous physical or mental exertion, which is hard work.

clue.text: Love the same sanctuary

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, written as O
as is means unchanged, just the same

explanation.surface: Affection gives the same refuge as ever.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile spot in a desert, figuratively any peaceful refuge.

clue.text: Eccentric boundlessly poker-faced environmentalist

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre or odd, so the letters are rearranged
without bounds, so the first and last letters of the word are dropped

explanation.surface: An odd, expressionless campaigner for the planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boundlessly' trims poker-faced to OKERFACE, which 'Eccentric' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An eco-freak is an informal, mildly mocking term for a zealous campaigner for green causes.

clue.text: Nothing eaten by greedy duck

indicators.note: eaten by means the nought goes inside the greedy word

parts.note: avid means eager or greedy
O resembles zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A hungry duck gobbles up nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' is the verb, to dodge, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck something is to dodge or evade it, so avoid.

clue.text: Bird is admitting ambiguous sexual identity

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the short word takes the other piece inside

parts.note: bi is short for bisexual

explanation.surface: A bird confesses to being unsure of its sexuality.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a down-curved bill.

clue.text: Remarkable development; quiet woman leads ordinary fellows on

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet
hen is slang for a woman, especially in Scotland
O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Something astonishing happens as a quiet woman ushers ordinary men forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A phenomenon is a remarkable event or person, something extraordinary that occurs.

clue.text: Obstinately continues appended note about cycling nun

indicators.note: about means the note's letters go round the other piece

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a note added to a letter

indicators.note: cycling means letters are moved round from the front of the word to the back

parts.note: a nun is called Sister

explanation.surface: A note tacked on about a nun who keeps on riding her bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' suggests a bicycle but means rotating letters, giving ERSIST; nuns are addressed by the title Sister.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist is to carry on firmly in spite of opposition.

clue.text: Hint at bone marrow going west losing mass

indicators.note: losing means dropping a letter from the reversed word
in an across answer going west means reading right to left

parts.note: medulla is the anatomical term for marrow
M is the symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A cook hints at a marrow bone fading and losing bulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going west' reverses MEDULLA to ALLUDEM; 'losing' drops the M.
explanation.definitionFit: To allude to something is to refer to it indirectly, which is to hint at it.
